title: About
text: BACKGROUND About My interests lie at the intersection of environmental economics, ecosystem science, and spatial data analysis. I am completing a Professional Science Master’s in Ecosystem Science & Sustainability (Carbon Management) at Colorado State University (degree expected January 2027), while pursuing an M.S. in Population, Resources & Environmental Economics at Shandong University (expected June 2027). I earned a B.A. in Economics from China University of Geosciences (Wuhan). My research experience includes regional life cycle assessment and costing of agricultural soil amendments, testing grazing-management scenarios with MEMS at LandEngine, and analyzing forest-cover change using Python and Google Earth Engine at CU Boulder’s ESIIL. Earlier projects involved panel-data econometrics, evolutionary game modeling, and agricultural input–output data integration. I am particularly interested in research that makes environmental and economic trade-offs explicit while accounting for differences across technologies, management practices, and landscapes. I hope to strengthen connections among these complementary methods through further research. Economics Costing · Incentives · Econometrics Environmental assessment LCA/LCC · GHG accounting Spatial & ecosystem analysis Python/GEE · MEMS workflows Research principles I aim to distinguish modeled scenarios from measured outcomes, spatial association from causation, and my specific contributions from collaborative project results. Methods and conclusions should be clear enough to support critical interpretation and real-world decisions. title: Research Projects
text: SELECTED RESEARCH EXPERIENCE Research projects Work across land-cover change, agricultural environmental–economic assessment, agroecosystem modeling, and quantitative economics. GEOSPATIAL ANALYSIS · 2026 Forest cover change across Colorado’s Front Range (2001–2021) Question. How did forest cover and land-cover transitions vary across elevation, and how were observed changes spatially associated with wildfire and development? Methods. Python, Google Earth Engine, NLCD land-cover data, burned-area layers, elevation data, area calculations, spatial overlay, and transition analysis. Findings. The team’s analysis found an approximately 19% decline in mapped forest cover over the period. Much of the mapped forest loss overlapped with burned areas; overlap alone does not establish causation. My contribution. Contributed to integration of geospatial datasets, analysis of land-cover change, visualizations, and collaborative interpretation. Research developed through CU Boulder’s Environmental Data Science Innovation & Impact Lab (ESIIL). Output: AGU 2026 poster accepted for presentation; collaborative research with team members and mentors. See portfolio overview LCA / LCC · AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS Environmental and economic assessment of synthetic humic substances Question. Under which production technologies, crop applications, and regional conditions might crop-residue-derived synthetic humic substances offer environmental and economic advantages? Methods. Regionalized life cycle assessment and life cycle costing across four production pathways, including production costs, monetized external environmental costs, agricultural-input substitution, and province-specific energy scenarios. Scope. Modeled applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple production in China, alongside comparisons of production pathways and electricity transition scenarios. My contribution. Evaluated environmental–economic trade-offs and regional heterogeneity as part of master’s research at Shandong University. Research presented at the Chinese Ecological Congress in October 2025. Detailed unpublished results are not posted here. See portfolio overview AGROECOSYSTEM MODELING · 2026 Grazing management and land-carbon model workflows Question. How can agricultural management scenarios be represented and interpreted consistently in model workflows and greenhouse gas accounting? Methods. Prepared site-specific inputs; tested continuous, low-rotation, and adaptive multi-paddock scenarios with the MEMS Grazing Scheduler; examined model outputs and documentation; worked with MEMS and DayCent workflows. My contribution. Model setup and testing, reproducible documentation, output review, and mapping of outputs to land-carbon accounting requirements during a research internship with LandEngine at Colorado State University. Internal models, inputs, and project repositories are not publicly reproduced. See portfolio overview Additional quantitative research ECONOMETRICS Wind power policy and corporate sustainability Two-way fixed-effects analysis of a 2009–2021 panel of 58 listed wind-power firms, with mechanism, heterogeneity, and robustness analyses. EVOLUTIONARY GAME THEORY Renewable Portfolio Standards Developed a tripartite evolutionary game model of government, renewable-energy producers, and consumers; used MATLAB numerical simulations and sensitivity analyses. AGRICULTURAL DATA China-specific FABIO framework Harmonized agricultural, biomass, economic, and environmental data and contributed to accounts and product-sector mappings for 84 agricultural products. CLUSTERING Industrial natural-gas customer heterogeneity Collaborative study of customer value classification using Gower dissimilarity and PAM clustering of mixed-type data. ESG ASSESSMENT Region-specific ESG evaluation Compared ESG frameworks and contributed to evaluation approaches incorporating local environmental and economic conditions.

title: Research Portfolio
text: SELECTED WORK & RESEARCH COMMUNICATION Research portfolio A curated look at real research questions, datasets, and analytical approaches. This page replaces the earlier illustrative sample charts with descriptions grounded in completed or ongoing projects. REMOTE SENSING & SPATIAL DATA 01 / Colorado Front Range forest change Data: NLCD land-cover maps for 2001 and 2021, burned-area datasets, and elevation models. Analysis: land-cover transitions, forest-type change, spatial overlap with burned areas, and elevation-related patterns using Python and Google Earth Engine. ~19% decrease in mapped forest cover in the team’s 2001–2021 study; an association, not a causal estimate Collaborative work through ESIIL. The presentation includes team and mentor contributions. Research figures and slide files are not republished here pending sharing review. Read the project summary ENVIRONMENTAL–ECONOMIC ASSESSMENT 02 / Synthetic humic substances for agricultural applications System: four crop-residue-derived production pathways and modeled applications in wheat, maize, rice, and apple systems in China. Assessment: life cycle impacts, internal production costs, monetized environmental externalities, crop-specific substitution scenarios, and regional electricity mixes. Interpretation: results depend on pathway assumptions, crop conditions, data sources, and system boundaries. Modeled economic impacts are not direct measurements of farm profitability. Research presented in Chinese at the 2025 Chinese Ecological Congress. An English summary is provided here; complete unpublished slides and underlying tables are not public. Read the project summary MODEL WORKFLOWS & SCENARIO TESTING 03 / Grazing-management scenarios Tools: MEMS Grazing Scheduler and related model workflows, with DayCent experience from training and project work. Tasks: management scenario input preparation, run testing, output interpretation, reproducible documentation, and carbon-accounting requirement review. Scope: these were ecosystem modeling and accounting tasks, not an independently developed ranch-profitability model. Only general work descriptions are shared; private project repositories and model input files remain restricted. Read the project summary Research materials and reproducibility Publicly shareable posters, figures, and code will be linked here after author and collaborator permissions are confirmed. The earlier synthetic demonstration dataset has been removed to distinguish teaching examples from actual research outputs.
